3. Kosala
Grandmother
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho rājānaṁ pasenadiṁ kosalaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: King Pasenadi of Kosala sat to one side, and the Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “handa kuto nu tvaṁ, mahārāja, āgacchasi divādivassā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Great King, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

segs.p: “Ayyikā me, bhante, kālaṅkatā jiṇṇā vuḍḍhā mahallikā addhagatā vayoanuppattā vīsavassasatikā jātiyā.
segs.e: “Sir, my grandmother has passed away. She was old, elderly and senior. She was advanced in years and had reached the final stage of life; she was a hundred and twenty years old.

segs.p: Ayyikā kho pana me, bhante, piyā hoti manāpā.
segs.e: But I loved my grandmother; she was dear to me.

segs.p: Hatthiratanena cepāhaṁ, bhante, labheyyaṁ ‘mā me ayyikā kālamakāsī’ti, hatthiratanampāhaṁ dadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: If by giving away the elephant-treasure I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.

segs.p: Assaratanena cepāhaṁ, bhante, labheyyaṁ ‘mā me ayyikā kālamakāsī’ti, assaratanampāhaṁ dadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: If by giving away the horse-treasure I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.

segs.p: Gāmavarena cepāhaṁ, bhante, labheyyaṁ ‘mā me ayyikā kālamakāsī’ti, gāmavarampāhaṁ dadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: If by giving away a prize village I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.

segs.p: Janapadapadesena cepāhaṁ, bhante, labheyyaṁ ‘mā me ayyikā kālamakāsī’ti, janapadapadesampāhaṁ dadeyyaṁ:
segs.e: If by giving away the whole country I could get my grandmother back, I’d do it.”

segs.p: “Sabbe sattā, mahārāja, maraṇadhammā maraṇapariyosānā maraṇaṁ anatītā”ti.
segs.e: “Great king, all sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.”
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing,
how well said this was by the Buddha:

segs.p: sabbe sattā maraṇadhammā maraṇapariyosānā maraṇaṁ anatītā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘All sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.’”
“That’s so true, Great King! That’s so true!

segs.p: Sabbe sattā maraṇadhammā maraṇapariyosānā maraṇaṁ anatītā.
segs.e: All sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, mahārāja, yāni kānici kumbhakārabhājanāni āmakāni ceva pakkāni ca sabbāni tāni bhedanadhammāni bhedanapariyosānāni bhedanaṁ anatītāni;
segs.e: It’s like the vessels made by potters. Whatever kind they are, whether baked or unbaked, all of them are liable to break apart. Breaking is their end; they’re not exempt from breakage.

segs.p: evameva kho, mahārāja, sabbe sattā maraṇadhammā maraṇapariyosānā maraṇaṁ anatītā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, all sentient beings are liable to die. Death is their end; they’re not exempt from death.”
That is what the Buddha said. …
“All beings will die,
for life ends in death.
They pass on according to their deeds,
reaping the fruits of good and bad.
Those who do bad go to hell,
and if you do good you go to heaven.
That’s why you should do good,
investing in the future life.
The good deeds of sentient beings
support them in the next world.”
Linked Discourses 3.23
3. Kosala
The World
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, King Pasenadi said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kati nu kho, bhante, lokassa dhammā uppajjamānā uppajjanti ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāyā”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, how many things arise in the world for its harm, suffering, and discomfort?”

segs.p: “Tayo kho, mahārāja, lokassa dhammā uppajjamānā uppajjanti ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya.
segs.e: “Great king, three things arise in the world for its harm, suffering, and discomfort.
What three?

segs.p: Lobho kho, mahārāja, lokassa dhammo, uppajjamāno uppajjati ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya.
segs.e: Greed,

segs.p: Doso kho, mahārāja, lokassa dhammo, uppajjamāno uppajjati ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya.
segs.e: hate,

segs.p: Moho kho, mahārāja, lokassa dhammo, uppajjamāno uppajjati ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāya.
segs.e: and delusion.

segs.p: Ime kho, mahārāja, tayo lokassa dhammā uppajjamānā uppajjanti ahitāya dukkhāya aphāsuvihārāyā”ti.
segs.e: These three things arise in the world for its harm, suffering, and discomfort.”
That is what the Buddha said. …
“When greed, hate, and delusion,
originate inside oneself,
they harm a person of wicked heart,
as a bamboo is destroyed by its own fruit.”
Linked Discourses 3.24
3. Kosala
Archery
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho rājā pasenadi kosalo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, King Pasenadi said to the Buddha,
“Sir, where should a gift be given?”
“Wherever your heart feels inspired, Great King.”
“But sir, where is a gift very fruitful?”

segs.p: “Aññaṁ kho etaṁ, mahārāja, kattha dānaṁ dātabbaṁ, aññaṁ panetaṁ kattha dinnaṁ mahapphalanti?
segs.e: “Where a gift should be given is one thing, Great King, but where a gift is very fruitful is another.

segs.p: Sīlavato kho, mahārāja, dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ, no tathā dussīle.
segs.e: A gift is very fruitful when it’s given to an ethical person, not so much to an unethical person.

segs.p: Tena hi, mahārāja, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā, te khameyya, tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
segs.e: Well then, Great King, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.
What do you think, Great King?

segs.p: idha tyassa yuddhaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ saṅgāmo samupabyūḷho.
segs.e: Suppose you were at war, ready to fight a battle.

segs.p: Atha āgaccheyya khattiyakumāro asikkhito akatahattho akatayoggo akatūpāsano bhīru chambhī utrāsī palāyī.
segs.e: Then along comes an aristocrat youth who is untrained, inexpert, unfit, inexperienced. And he’s fearful, scared, nervous, quick to flee.

segs.p: Bhareyyāsi taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca te tādisena purisenā”ti?
segs.e: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

segs.p: “Nāhaṁ, bhante, bhareyyaṁ taṁ purisaṁ, na ca me attho tādisena purisenā”ti.
segs.e: “No, sir, I would have no use for such a man.”
“What about a brahmin youth,
a peasant youth,
or a menial youth who was similar?”

segs.p: na ca me attho tādisena purisenā”ti.
segs.e: “No, sir, I would have no use for such a man.”
“What do you think, Great King?

segs.p: idha tyassa yuddhaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ saṅgāmo samupabyūḷho.
segs.e: Suppose you were at war, ready to fight a battle.

segs.p: Atha āgaccheyya khattiyakumāro susikkhito katahattho katayoggo katūpāsano abhīru acchambhī anutrāsī apalāyī.
segs.e: Then along comes an aristocrat youth who is trained, expert, fit, experienced. And he’s fearless, brave, bold, standing his ground.

segs.p: Bhareyyāsi taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca te tādisena purisenā”ti?
segs.e: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

segs.p: “Bhareyyāhaṁ, bhante, taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca me tādisena purisenā”ti.
segs.e: “Yes, sir, I would have a use for such a man.”
“What about a brahmin youth,
a peasant youth,

segs.p: atha āgaccheyya suddakumāro susikkhito katahattho katayoggo katūpāsano abhīru acchambhī anutrāsī apalāyī.
segs.e: or a menial youth who was similar?

segs.p: Bhareyyāsi taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca te tādisena purisenā”ti?
segs.e: Would you employ such a man? Would he be of any use to you?”

segs.p: “Bhareyyāhaṁ, bhante, taṁ purisaṁ, attho ca me tādisena purisenā”ti.
segs.e: “Yes, sir, I would have a use for such a man.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, mahārāja, yasmā kasmā cepi kulā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti, so ca hoti pañcaṅgavippahīno pañcaṅgasamannāgato, tasmiṁ dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ hoti.
segs.e: “In the same way, a gift to anyone who has given up five factors and possesses five factors is very fruitful, no matter what family they’ve gone forth from.
What are the five factors they’ve given up?

segs.p: Kāmacchando pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti.
segs.e: Sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
These are the five factors they’ve given up.
What are the five factors they possess?

segs.p: Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekkhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: The entire spectrum of an adept’s ethics, immersion, wisdom, freedom, and knowledge and vision of freedom.
These are the five factors they possess.
I say that a gift to anyone who has given up these five factors and possesses these five factors is very fruitful.”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Any youth skilled at archery,
powerful and vigorous,
would be employed by a king going to war—
one is not a coward by reason of birth.
Just so, whoever is settled
in the qualities of patience and gentleness,
an intelligent person with noble conduct,
should be venerated even if they’re low born.
You should build lovely hermitages
and settle learned people in them.
You should set up water supplies in barren regions
and passages in places hard to travel.
Food, drink, edibles,
clothes, and lodgings
should be given to the upright ones,
with a clear and confident heart.
The thundering rain cloud,
its hundred peaks wreathed in lightning,
pours down over the rich earth,
soaking the uplands and valleys.
So too an astute person,
faithful and learned,
should prepare a meal to satisfy
supplicants with food and drink.
Rejoicing, they strew gifts about,
saying, ‘Give! Give!’
For that is their thunder,
like rain sent from the heavens.
That stream of merit so abundant
showers down on the giver.”

3. Kosala
The Simile of the Mountain
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho rājānaṁ pasenadiṁ kosalaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: King Pasenadi of Kosala sat to one side, and the Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “handa kuto nu tvaṁ, mahārāja, āgacchasi divā divassā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Great King, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

segs.p: “Yāni tāni, bhante, raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ issariyamadamattānaṁ kāmagedhapariyuṭṭhitānaṁ janapadatthāvariyappattānaṁ mahantaṁ pathavimaṇḍalaṁ abhivijiya ajjhāvasantānaṁ rājakaraṇīyāni bhavanti, tesu khvāhaṁ, etarahi ussukkamāpanno”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, there are anointed aristocratic kings who are infatuated with authority, and obsessed with greed for sensual pleasures. They have attained stability in the country, occupying a vast conquered territory. Today I have been busy fulfilling the duties of such kings.”
“What do you think, Great King?

segs.p: idha te puriso āgaccheyya puratthimāya disāya saddhāyiko paccayiko.
segs.e: Suppose a trustworthy and dependable man were to come from the east.
He’d approach you and say:

segs.p: ‘yagghe, mahārāja, jāneyyāsi, ahaṁ āgacchāmi puratthimāya disāya.
segs.e: ‘Please, Great King, you should know this. I come from the east.

segs.p: Tatthaddasaṁ mahantaṁ pabbataṁ abbhasamaṁ, sabbe pāṇe nippothento āgacchati.
segs.e: There I saw a big mountain that reached the clouds. And it was coming this way, crushing all creatures.

segs.p: Yaṁ te, mahārāja, karaṇīyaṁ, taṁ karohī’ti.
segs.e: So then, Great King, do what you must!’

segs.p: Atha dutiyo puriso āgaccheyya pacchimāya disāya …pe…
segs.e: Then a second trustworthy and dependable man were to come from the west …

segs.p: atha tatiyo puriso āgaccheyya uttarāya disāya …
segs.e: a third from the north …

segs.p: atha catuttho puriso āgaccheyya dakkhiṇāya disāya saddhāyiko paccayiko.
segs.e: and a fourth from the south.
He’d approach you and say:

segs.p: ‘yagghe, mahārāja, jāneyyāsi, ahaṁ āgacchāmi dakkhiṇāya disāya.
segs.e: ‘Please, Great King, you should know this. I come from the south.

segs.p: Tatthaddasaṁ mahantaṁ pabbataṁ abbhasamaṁ sabbe pāṇe nippothento āgacchati.
segs.e: There I saw a big mountain that reached the clouds. And it was coming this way, crushing all creatures.

segs.p: Yaṁ te, mahārāja, karaṇīyaṁ taṁ karohī’ti.
segs.e: So then, Great King, do what you must!’

segs.p: Evarūpe te, mahārāja, mahati mahabbhaye samuppanne dāruṇe manussakkhaye dullabhe manussatte kimassa karaṇīyan”ti?
segs.e: Should such a dire threat arise—a grim loss of human life, when human birth is so rare—what would you do?”

segs.p: “Evarūpe me, bhante, mahati mahabbhaye samuppanne dāruṇe manussakkhaye dullabhe manussatte kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya aññatra samacariyāya aññatra kusalakiriyāya aññatra puññakiriyāyā”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what could I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”

segs.p: “Ārocemi kho te, mahārāja, paṭivedemi kho te, mahārāja, adhivattati kho taṁ, mahārāja, jarāmaraṇaṁ.
segs.e: “I tell you, Great King, I announce to you: old age and death are advancing upon you.

segs.p: Adhivattamāne ce te, mahārāja, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyan”ti?
segs.e: Since old age and death are advancing upon you, what would you do?”

segs.p: “Adhivattamāne ca me, bhante, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāya?
segs.e: “Sir, what can I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?

segs.p: Yāni tāni, bhante, raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ issariyamadamattānaṁ kāmagedhapariyuṭṭhitānaṁ janapadatthāvariyappattānaṁ mahantaṁ pathavimaṇḍalaṁ abhivijiya ajjhāvasantānaṁ hatthiyuddhāni bhavanti;
segs.e: Sir, there are anointed aristocratic kings who are infatuated with authority, and obsessed with greed for sensual pleasures. They have attained stability in the country, occupying a vast conquered territory. Such kings engage in battles of elephants,

segs.p: tesampi, bhante, hatthiyuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
Yānipi tāni, bhante, raññaṁ khattiyānaṁ muddhāvasittānaṁ …pe…

segs.e: cavalry,
chariots,
or infantry.

segs.p: tesampi, bhante, pattiyuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
segs.e: But there is no place, no domain for such battles when old age and death are advancing.

segs.p: Santi kho pana, bhante, imasmiṁ rājakule mantino mahāmattā, ye pahonti āgate paccatthike mantehi bhedayituṁ.
segs.e: In this royal court there are ministers of wise counsel who are capable of dividing an approaching enemy by wise counsel.

segs.p: Tesampi, bhante, mantayuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
segs.e: But there is no place, no domain for such diplomatic battles when old age and death are advancing.

segs.p: Saṁvijjati kho pana, bhante, imasmiṁ rājakule pahūtaṁ hiraññasuvaṇṇaṁ bhūmigatañceva vehāsaṭṭhañca, yena mayaṁ pahoma āgate paccatthike dhanena upalāpetuṁ.
segs.e: In this royal court there is abundant gold, both coined and uncoined, stored above and below ground. Using this wealth we can bribe an approaching enemy.

segs.p: Tesampi, bhante, dhanayuddhānaṁ natthi gati natthi visayo adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe.
segs.e: But there is no place, no domain for such monetary battles when old age and death are advancing.

segs.p: Adhivattamāne ca me, bhante, jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāyā”ti?
segs.e: When old age and death are advancing, what can I do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”
“That’s so true, Great King! That’s so true!

segs.p: Adhivattamāne jarāmaraṇe kimassa karaṇīyaṁ aññatra dhammacariyāya samacariyāya kusalakiriyāya puññakiriyāyā”ti?
segs.e: When old age and death are advancing, what can you do but practice the teachings, practice morality, doing skillful and good actions?”
That is what the Buddha said.
Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Suppose there were vast mountains
of solid rock pressing against the sky
drawing in from all sides
and crushing the four quarters.
So too old age and death
advance upon all living creatures—
aristocrats, brahmins, peasants,
menials, corpse-workers, and scavengers.
They spare nothing.
They crush all beneath them.
There’s nowhere for elephants to take a stand,
nor chariots nor infantry.
They can’t be defeated
by diplomatic battles or by wealth.
That’s why an astute person,
seeing what’s good for themselves,
being wise, would place faith
in the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.
Whoever lives by the teaching
in body, speech, and mind,
is praised in this life
and departs to rejoice in heaven.”
The Linked Discourses with the Kosalan are complete.
